text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - German debt prices continued their jaunt higher on Monday with both June futures and cash 10-year Bunds comfortably above the 102.00 level in late trade. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 102.28, up 0.51 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures closed higher, buoyed by comments from Chancellor Gordon Brown ruling out Britain rejoining the ERM, which boosted sterling. Strength in Bunds and a firmer tone in Treasuries were also supportive. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 114-15/32, up 08/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - PIBOR surges to end at day highs along with bond futures, driven by weekend opinion polls turned in favour of centre-right election victory, foreign buying, short covering late in MATIF day, traders say. 10-year cash ylds fall. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.30 up 0.56 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian Btps holding up firmly in end of day trade with futures pushing to stand 40 basis points higher after seesawing on EU report over Italy's fiscal discipline. Finance Ministers called Italy's 1996 spending controls insufficient and urged permanent deficit cuts. But more positive impulses coming other bond markets. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.76 up 0.46 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries edge higher, near end leads. Fund demand for three-year notes seen, with some some 10-yr offered against. Steeper curve still seen, Greenspan dents May 20 hike odds. April retail sales Tues seen weak, longs carefully built ahead. Cheaper dollar/yen may have bolstered, not hurt demand.The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-12/32, up 5/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.87 percent.

JAPAN - Key June Japanese goverment bonds (JGB) futures ended easier, weighed down by firm Tokyo stocks despite strong yen. Afternoon remark by LDP's Taku Yamasaki that Japan rate rise would undermine economy gave brief support, but rally stopped short as comment was not denial of higher rates, but aimed at curbing yen's sharp rise. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 123.34, down 0.31 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
